bar_type_drawing_symbols.description: Single-letter symbols used on drawings/schedules to denote reinforcement type/grade, by historical period. See 02_engineering_knowledge.json material_property_periods for the full period-by-period mapping.

symbols_seen.R: Plain/deformed grade 250 (varies slightly by era) — BS4466:1981 onward
symbols_seen.T: Type 2 deformed bars, grade 460/425 or Ductility B (varies by era)
symbols_seen.X: Not covered by other listed symbols / type defined in design or contract specification
symbols_seen.S: Stainless reinforcement (1985-2004 era) OR a not-otherwise-listed type (BS8666 era) — symbol meaning shifted between eras, see source
symbols_seen.W: Plain reinforcement to BS4482 (1985-2004) OR Ductility A/B deformed Type 2 to BS4449 (BS8666 era) — meaning shifted between eras
symbols_seen.D: Type 1 deformed reinforcement to BS4482 (1985-2004) OR plain round to BS4482/fabric to BS4483 (BS8666 era)
symbols_seen.F: Deformed Type 2 to BS4482 or Ductility A of BS4449 (BS8666 era only)
symbols_seen.B: Specified grade/type of stainless steel to BS6744 (BS8666 era only)
symbols_seen.H: Used throughout the separately-processed Columns/Walls/Foundations/Staircases chapter (e.g. 'H20', 'H10') for high-yield deformed bar. INFERRED equivalent to BS8666-era high-yield deformed bar; not itself defined in this appendix (see gaps file).

bar_type_drawing_symbols.caution: The same letter symbol (S, W, D, T, R, X) can mean a DIFFERENT bar type/grade depending on which historical period's table applies. A generator reproducing period-accurate drawings MUST select the symbol table by the target drawing's era/code, never assume a fixed universal mapping.

bar_callout_notation_general.example: 4 H20 19  =  4 bars, high-yield deformed, 20mm diameter, bar mark 19
bar_callout_notation_general.example_with_spacing: 15 H8 20 200  =  15 bars, high-yield deformed, 8mm dia, bar mark 20, at 200mm centres
bar_callout_notation_general.wall_zone_suffix_example: 20H10-63-150N1  =  20 bars, H10, bar mark 63, at 150mm centres, Near Face, layer 1
bar_callout_notation_general.source_note: This callout pattern is DIRECTLY STATED in the previously processed member chapter (pp.88-127), not this appendix; included here because it is the notation that Appendix B's shape-code/dimension data ultimately feeds (the number+diameter+mark+spacing callout references a schedule row keyed by bar mark, and the schedule row's shape code + A-E dimensions come from this appendix's Table catalogue).

bar_bending_schedule_fields.description: Implied schedule row structure, reconstructed from the shape-code table's column headings and the constraint language ('Neither A nor... shall be less than P').

fields.meaning: unique reference number tying a schedule row to drawing callouts
2-digit code from the standard catalogue (00-99), selects the length formula and the dimension-letter template (A,B,C,D,E)
primary controlled dimension; not a free/tolerance dimension unless code 99 says otherwise
further dimensions as required by the shape code template; the one shown in parentheses in the standard table is the free/tolerance-absorbing dimension
computed via the shape code's length formula from A..E, d, and r
which member/location this bar belongs to (as seen in the member chapter's per-member tables, e.g. 'COLUMN REF' or 'FLIGHT B')

bar_bending_schedule_fields.fact_status: INFERRED structure (the schedule columns themselves are not shown as a table image in this appendix extract) but individual field meanings are DIRECTLY STATED elsewhere in the shape-code descriptions and constraint text.

shape_diagram_drawing_conventions.dimension_letter_convention: Each shape uses up to 5 dimension letters A, B, C, D, E laid out along the bar's segments in the schematic. A dimension shown in parentheses, e.g. (C), is the free/tolerance dimension — the fabricator/detailer allows deviation to land there rather than on the other controlled dimensions.

bend_geometry_symbols.r: minimum scheduling radius (internal bend radius), read from Table B.1 by bar size
bend_geometry_symbols.R: an explicit/design-specified bend radius, used instead of the standard r in some shapes (e.g. shape 12)
bend_geometry_symbols.d: nominal bar diameter, used directly in every length-adjustment term of every formula (bend allowance deduction)

special_shape_conventions.shape_47_and_51_and_63: Offer both an exact formula and an alternative 'minimized' formula expressed directly in terms of bar diameter (e.g. max(16d,160)) for when the free dimensions (C)/(D) are to be minimized rather than solved from stated A/B — i.e., two valid ways to dimension the same shape depending on detailer intent.
special_shape_conventions.shape_67: Refers out to BS8666 Clause 10 rather than giving an in-manual formula — an explicit DEPENDENCY on an external code clause not reproduced here.
special_shape_conventions.shape_98: Explicitly noted as an isometric sketch convention — used for genuinely 3-dimensional bar shapes (e.g. spatial cranks) that cannot be shown in a single 2D elevation.
special_shape_conventions.shape_99: The escape-hatch convention: any shape not matching 00-98 must be drawn as a fully dimensioned sketch with an explicit free dimension in parentheses; used, per this manual's earlier member chapter, for special/one-off details (e.g. Model Detail shapes referenced by name rather than code, such as MC2, MW3, MF5).

note_labels_seen_in_member_chapter: N = Near face, F = Far face (wall reinforcement layer notation, 6.5.2)
T = Top, B = Bottom (column/footing bar layer notation, e.g. '8 H16 04 250 T')
UB = Undefined/unbanded? or 'U-bar' shorthand — appears as suffix in schedules (e.g. '5 H10 10 200 (UB)') — meaning not explicitly defined in the extracted member chapter text; flagged as a gap

Model Detail codes (e.g. MC1-MC6, MW1-MW4, MRW1-MRW3, MF1-MF5, MST1-MST2) act as named, reusable standard-detail references cross-linking a specific bar arrangement to a generic detail rather than redrawing it per instance
